{
    r := [];

        invariant 0 <= i <= |s1|

    {
        r := r + [s1[i], s2[i], s3[i]];

reasoning_content:
I notice the invariant has an off-by-one in its index, which could cause either the postcondition to fail or the invariant preservation step to fail across loop iterations. I'm tracing through the exact line numbers to pinpoint which invariant clause is responsible.

Since the weaker bound `k < i-1` doesn't account for the newly added element at index `i-1`, preservation breaks—the loop step can't justify the forall property holds for the new element. That points to preservation failure at the forall invariant line as the primary error.
